text: 1. On March 4, 2023, at approximately 9:20 p.m., a collision occurred at the intersection of Mission Street and 14th Avenue in San Francisco, California, involving a Green Valley Logistics, Inc. (“Green Valley”) 2020 Freightliner box truck and a blue Honda Civic operated by Maria Lopez (“Lopez”). 2. At the time of the incident, the Green Valley vehicle, California license plate 9TRK220, was being operated by Daniel Reed (“Reed”), a commercial driver employed by Green Valley. 3. Weather conditions at the time of the incident were rainy, with steady precipitation and wet roadway surfaces. Visibility was reduced due to rain and glare from street lighting. 4. The intersection of Mission Street and 14th Avenue is controlled by traffic signals for all directions of travel, with dedicated left-turn phases for Mission Street. 5. According to Reed and initial observations, Lopez was traveling eastbound on Mission Street at an estimated speed of between forty-five (45) and fifty (50) miles per hour in a posted thirty-five (35) mile-per-hour zone. 6. Reed was traveling southbound on 14th Avenue at approximately twenty-five (25) miles per hour, intending to proceed straight through the intersection. 7. Reed states that as he approached the intersection, the traffic signal facing southbound traffic on 14th Avenue was solid green, with no yellow or red indication. He maintains that he entered the intersection lawfully on a green light. 8. Reed further reports that as he entered the intersection, the Honda Civic driven by Lopez entered from the west, traveling eastbound on Mission Street against a solid red signal or late yellow that had already changed, and that the Civic did not slow prior to entering the intersection. 9. Reed applied his brakes and attempted to steer to the right to avoid impact; however, due to the wet roadway and the speed of the Civic, the front of the Green Valley truck contacted the driver’s side front quarter panel of the Civic in the middle of the intersection. 10. Reed observed at least one additional adult occupant seated in the front passenger seat of the Honda Civic at the time of impact. 11. Following the collision, Reed exited his truck and approached the Civic. He observed Lopez standing outside the driver’s side door without assistance and walking unassisted on the sidewalk. He noted that the driver appeared upset but was speaking in full sentences, using her mobile phone. 12. Reed did not observe any seat belt across Lopez’s torso or lap when she exited the vehicle and believes she was not restrained at the time of the collision. 13. Reed reports that Lopez repeatedly stated at the scene that she was “okay” and that she did not want an ambulance. No ambulance transport of Lopez from the scene was observed by Reed or by  other Green Valley personnel. 14. A San Francisco Police Department officer responded to the scene, obtained information from the parties, and released Reed after completing a preliminary investigation. 15. The Green Valley truck sustained visible damage to the front bumper and grille but remained operable and was driven from the scene. The Honda Civic sustained damage primarily to the front driver’s side fender and door area. 16. Lopez advised Reed and the responding officer that she was returning home from dinner prior to the incident. She did not report that she was traveling from work. DRIVER EMPLOYMENT AND ASSIGNMENT 17. At the time of the incident, Reed was a full-time employee of Green Valley assigned to the San Francisco local delivery route. 18. On March 4, 2023, Reed completed his scheduled delivery route at approximately 8:30 p.m. and was released from duty. At the time of the collision, he was driving the Green Valley truck home for personal convenience and was not engaged in any active delivery, pickup, or other business purpose on behalf of Green Valley. 19. Company records reflect that Reed had no prior preventable motor vehicle collisions during his employment with Green Valley. 20. A later audit of Reed’s file confirmed that he had been involved in a preventable rear-end collision with another vehicle while operating a Green Valley truck on February 2, 2020, in Oakland, California, for which he received remedial training. CLAIM AND MEDICAL INFORMATION 21. On March 21, 2023, Lopez reported a bodily injury claim to Green Valley’s insurance carrier, stating that she sustained neck and back injuries as a result of the March 4, 2023 incident. 22. In a recorded telephone statement taken by the insurer on March 22, 2023, Lopez stated that she did not seek any medical treatment on the night of the collision and that she first saw a medical provider at an urgent care clinic on March 20, 2023, approximately sixteen (16) days after the incident. 23. Lopez further reported in the recorded statement that she attended “around six” physical therapy sessions over a period of approximately one month following the urgent care visit and then stopped treatment when her symptoms improved. 24. Lopez advised the insurer that she missed “about three days” of work from her job as a dental assistant following the incident and then returned to full-time duties. 25. As of September 1, 2023, medical bills submitted to and processed by the insurer in connection with Lopez’s claim totaled Fourteen Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars ($14,250.00), consisting primarily of urgent care visits, diagnostic imaging, and a limited course of physical therapy. 26. The insurer’s property damage estimate for the Honda Civic identified repairable damage to the driver’s side front fender, driver’s door, and related components, with a total repair cost of Seven Thousand Four Hundred Dollars ($7,400.00). The vehicle was not declared a total loss, and its actual cash value immediately prior to the incident was estimated at Eight Thousand Five Hundred Dollars  ($8,500.00). 27. In her recorded statement, Lopez confirmed that she was the registered owner of the Honda Civic and that there were “two people” in the vehicle at the time of the incident, including herself and an adult friend. PRIOR ACCIDENT HISTORY 28. During the recorded telephone statement, Lopez initially stated that she had not been involved in any motor vehicle accidents in the past ten (10) years. 29. When confronted with claim database information, Lopez acknowledged that she had previously been involved in a rear-end motor vehicle collision on June 10, 2018, in San Francisco, California, in which she complained of neck soreness and for which she sought medical treatment. 30. Claim database records further reflect that Lopez submitted another bodily injury claim arising from a separate motor vehicle incident in 2019 in Daly City, California, in which she alleged back pain. Documentation for the 2019 incident has not yet been obtained. CONCLUSIONS AND PRELIMINARY LIABILITY ASSESSMENT 31. Based on the information currently available, including the driver’s statement, scene conditions, and the recorded statement of Lopez, Green Valley’s Risk Management Department preliminarily concludes that the primary cause of the collision was Lopez’s failure to stop for a red traffic signal or late yellow at the intersection of Mission Street and 14th Avenue while traveling at an excessive speed on a wet roadway. 32. The Department further concludes that Reed entered the intersection on a green light at a reasonable speed for the conditions and that there is no evidence he was distracted, impaired, or otherwise unfit to operate the vehicle at the time of the incident. 33. Green Valley’s preliminary position is that any injuries and damages claimed by Lopez are inconsistent with her delayed treatment, limited course of therapy, and statements regarding her brief time off work, and that her claimed losses are significantly greater than what would be expected from the nature of the impact and the repairable damage to the Honda Civic. 34. Green Valley reserves all rights to supplement or amend this Incident Report and preliminary liability assessment as additional information becomes available, including police reports, medical records, witness statements, and expert opinions.
